name: Positioning Chain Coherence

positioning.oneLineSummary: Checks whether alternatives, capabilities, value, best-fit customers, and category form one evidenced and falsifiable chain.
positioning.productLabel: Positioning-Coherence Lens — product synthesis from April Dunford's public method
notAClaimOf: one positioning chain covering incompatible segments

attribution.display: Product synthesis from April Dunford's public positioning method

neutralParaphrase: Join the five component outputs without averaging away contradictions: each capability must be differentiated against a real alternative, enable a verified outcome, matter disproportionately to an identifiable customer, and become easier to understand in the chosen category. Record breaks, alternative chains, and falsifiers.

locator.value: Five components, dependency order, and Janna Systems example
Official five-component and unique-value learning outcomes

requiredConditions: OA2-02 through OA2-06 have independent outputs.
Evidence provenance and hypothesis status are preserved.

requiredEvidence.description: Independent evidence, judgment, counterevidence, and unknowns from each five-component card.
Explicit links from alternative through capability, value, best-fit characteristic, and category.
Observations that would break each link or support a competing positioning chain.

decisionQuestions: Does every claimed value trace to a differentiated capability and real alternative?
Do best-fit characteristics explain who cares and who does not?
Does category illuminate rather than redefine the value?
Which link is weakest, contradicted, or merely hypothesized?
positiveSignals: The full chain is supported by repeated customer and operating evidence.
Contradictory segments are separated rather than averaged.
The weakest links and falsifiers are explicit.
An alternative chain can be tested without rewriting history.
redFlags: Category or value was chosen first and other components were backfilled.
A polished statement hides missing customer evidence.
Different segments require incompatible alternatives and value.
The chain cannot state what evidence would falsify it.
disconfirmingEvidence: Strong individual components do not connect into one buying rationale.
Customers buy for a different value than management believes.
The best-fit segment has weak retention or economics.
A competing chain explains wins more consistently.
contraindications: Do not collapse component confidence into one opaque score.
Do not force contradictions to resolve.
Do not equate internal consensus with external validation.

instructions: Construct one or more explicit evidence chains.
Mark support, contradiction, hypothesis, and missing links.
Compare alternative chains by customer evidence.
Conclude coherent, partially coherent, contradictory, or insufficient.

deterministicRule.prohibition: The language model must not convert the chain into an opaque positioning score.

sourceReliability.high: All component links have independent customer and operating evidence.

evidenceStrength.medium: Most links supported with one weak point.
evidenceStrength.high: Repeated buying and use behavior supports the complete chain.

evidenceCoverage.high: All links, segments, counterchains, falsifiers, and provenance covered.

applicabilityConfidence.high: GTM materially depends on one or more testable positioning chains.

empiricalQualifications: Coherence is necessary but not sufficient for GTM success.
Customer behavior and competition change over time.

rights.notes: The evidence graph is product synthesis from public author doctrine.
